messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The pattern {head=F, ant=NAM} is found in the data." -- cites: E5 (Figure 4): observation "The pattern {head=F, ant=NAM} is explicitly shown in the Conditional FP-Tree."
2. "The probability of finding the pattern {head=F, ant=NAM} in the data is not explicitly stated." -- cites: E1 (Section A): quote "X 1 = { ana-type=NAM, ant-type=NAM, headmatch=F } , C ( X 1 ) = 0"

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section A, page 13): X 1 = { ana-type=NAM, ant-type=NAM, headmatch=F } , C ( X 1 ) = 0 X 2 = { ana-type=NAM, ant-type=NAM, headmatch=T } , C ( X 2 ) = 1 X 3 = { ana-type=NAM, ant-type=NOM, headmatch=F } , C ( X 3 ) = 0 • A = { ana-type=NAM, ant-type=NAM, headmatch=F, head-match=T, ant-type=NOM } , • support ( a i , 0) a i ∈ A = { 2,1,2,0,1 } , e.g. “anatype=NAM” appeared two times in noncoreferring ( C ( X i ) = 0 ) samples, If we sort A based on a i ’s frequencies, i.e. support ( a i , 0) + support ( a i , 1) , the ordering of A ’s items will remain the same. Now, we need to go through the samples again to build the tree. The FP-Tree construction steps after adding each of the above samples is demonstrated in Figure 1 . ana-type=NAM, anttype=NAM, head-match=F, head-match=T, and ant-type=NOM are abbreviated as ana=NAM, ant=NAM, head=F, head=T, and ant=NOM, respectively in Figures 1 and 2 . Figure 2 shows the resulted FP-Tree in which corresponding support values for both classes, i.e. zero and one, are also included in each node.
[E5] (figure, Figure 4, page 14) (image attached): Figure 4 : Conditional FP-Tree for the p = { head=F , ant=NAM } pattern.
Words printed in the figure: ROOT ana=NAM (1,0) ant=NAM (1,0) head=F (1,0) head=T (0,1) head=F (1,0) ant=NOM (1,0) [image]

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E5 (Figure 4) explicitly shows the pattern {head=F, ant=NAM} in the Conditional FP-Tree.

The evidence in E1 (Section A) does not explicitly state the probability of finding the pattern {head=F, ant=NAM} in the data. It only provides the count of occurrences for the pattern {head=F, ant=NAM} in the data, which is 0.
